mutations.name: a probe TIMEOUT is reported as an unbound responder instead of an unchecked axis
mutations.cell: CELL C4: a probe TIMEOUT grades `unknown`, never `unbound` (a timeout is not the broker saying nothing is bound)

mutations.name: a reply that carries no readable verdict is promoted to bound merely for having arrived (the pgrep error)
mutations.cell: CELL C9: a reply with NO readable verdict falls to `unknown`, not to `bound`

mutations.name: a lease that has not reached ready is graded as a bound responder
mutations.cell: CELL B2b: a lease that is CLAIMED but not READY grades `unbound` (the 22-hour state: the slot is taken, the responder is not up)

mutations.name: a responder whose readState throws answers bound instead of unknown
mutations.cell: CELL C1: a DELIVERY responder that cannot read its lease answers `unknown`, never `bound`

mutations.name: a reply naming a different plane than the one asked about is adopted as that plane's answer
mutations.find: if (typeof plane !== "string" || !isLivenessPlane(plane) || plane !== expectPlane) return undefined;
mutations.cell: CELL D11: a reply naming a DIFFERENT plane than the one asked about is rejected, not adopted

mutations.name: an unrecognised responder value in a reply is accepted rather than refused
mutations.find:
if (responder !== "bound" && responder !== "unbound" && responder !== "stale" && responder !== "unknown") return undefined;
  return { plane, responder };
mutations.replace:
if (typeof responder !== "string") return undefined;
  return { plane, responder: responder as ResponderState };
mutations.cell: CELL D12: a reply with an unrecognised responder value is rejected (it grades `unknown`, never `bound`)

mutations.name: the responder answers any reply target, not only one under the sender's own subtree
mutations.cell: CELL D4b: a probe whose reply target is ANOTHER peer's lane is NOT answered (no confused deputy)

mutations.name: the responder reports a plane it was not asked about, so an answer about delivery can arrive for a question about the manager
mutations.replace: const answer = { plane: plane === "manager" ? "delivery" : "manager", responder } as LivenessAnswer;
mutations.cell: CELL B1: with a responder bound, the peer's MANAGER probe returns `bound`

mutations.name: a peer may probe under another principal's identity slots because the subject stops pinning the caller
mutations.cell: CELL D2: a peer CANNOT publish a probe under another principal's identity slots

mutations.name: an agent is granted the responder's serve filter and can answer a peer's probe for a plane it does not own
mutations.find: const livenessReplies = LIVENESS_PLANES.map((plane) => `${livenessSubject(space, plane, pr.owner, pr.actor)}.>`);
mutations.replace: const livenessReplies = [...LIVENESS_PLANES.map((plane) => `${livenessSubject(space, plane, pr.owner, pr.actor)}.>`), ...LIVENESS_PLANES.map((plane) => livenessServeFilter(space, plane))];
mutations.cell: CELL D3: a peer CANNOT subscribe the responder's SERVE filter (it cannot answer for a plane)

mutations.name: the supervisor's reply grant widens off the reply leaf so it could forge a probe as a peer
mutations.cell: CELL E3: the supervisor's reply grant is bounded to the `.reply.` leaf - it cannot publish a probe AS a peer

mutations.name: the delivery plane's serve filter is granted to the supervisor too, so planes no longer answer only for themselves
mutations.cell: CELL E2: the `supervisor` CANNOT serve the DELIVERY plane (each plane answers for itself)

mutations.name: a plane outside the closed set is answered instead of refused
mutations.cell: CELL D9: a peer asking about a plane outside the closed set is REFUSED, not answered

mutations.name: the answer carries the lease holder alongside presence, leaking identity to a non-owner peer
mutations.replace: const answer = { plane, responder, holder: this.card.id } as LivenessAnswer;
mutations.cell: CELL D8: the wire answer carries EXACTLY {plane, responder} - no holder, pid, root, instance id or roster
